analysis:
Code change: `darkbloom restart` (RestartCommand.swift:37-40) now wraps stop+relaunch in the new `ServiceDrain.relaunchDrainedProvider` (ServiceDrain+Recovery.swift, added after line 37). That helper runs `defer { rearm(explicitConfig) }`, so `ServiceDrain.rearmWatchdog` runs on success and on any failure after the drain commits. Before, the re-arm sat after the relaunch and was skipped when the relaunch threw, leaving the provider down with crash recovery off. The drain-timeout fence in `prepare` is untouched because it throws before the closure runs. Security view: this restores availability (T-010 and T-043 context) and adds no new authority. The re-arm re-enables the existing watchdog LaunchAgent, which is the same replaceable-binary rollback authority T-043 already covers. It re-uses `explicitConfig`, so there is no new input.

Not visible and worth a later check: the `rearmWatchdog` body. It now also runs on the `LaunchAgentError.notInstalled` path (RestartCommand.swift:41), and the next pass should confirm it does not install or arm a watchdog for a provider that is not installed. The default `rearm` closure is injectable, which is a test seam only.

Docs: `docs/provider/cli-reference.md` appears only as head text with no diff. It describes the existing CLI, paths, env passthrough, the opt-in App Attest worker candidate flag (TB-011), cache and KEK items (T-041), and logout and unenroll semantics. I saw no claims that weaken or contradict the threat model (no new endpoints or receipt-policy claims), and no security findings arise from the doc text.
